upstream.adaptation: The pointwise trace-norm proof and maximum-principle assembly are adapted for a nonpositive initial scalar bound. The original positive-scalar finite-lifetime theorem is not used as a finite-extinction theorem.

closed_surface_adaptation.change: Adapt the smooth pullback construction from diffeomorphisms to maps with injective differential. Use the existing finite-dimensional positive-definite boundedness proof. Localize the upstream all-real-time volume variation theorem by a smooth time map, keeping the upstream integration and chart-gluing proof unchanged.

mathematical_reference.title: Width and finite extinction time of Ricci flow

validated_scope.scalar: A closed boundaryless three-dimensional smooth Ricci flow satisfying IsSolutionOn and an initial scalar bound -3/(2*C), C > 0, has scalar curvature at least -3/(2*(t+C)) on each admissible compact smooth time slab. No initial curvature-operator lower bound is assumed.
validated_scope.regularity: Scalar evolution and maximum-principle regularity are derived from the upstream solution predicate, whose geometric equation is metric variation by -2 Ricci. The theorem does not construct this solution from initial data.
validated_scope.minimum: The scalar minimum is the infimum of the actual scalar-curvature range and is proved to be attained on a nonempty compact manifold.
validated_scope.normalization: The initial bound -6 gives -6/(1+4*t), matching the existing extinction trace.
validated_scope.surface: The pullback metric and Ricci matrices use the actual manifold derivative of a fixed map from the Euclidean parameter plane. Positive induced determinant gives the local density variation. An integral formula on a parameter patch follows under explicit measurable, integrable and dominated-derivative hypotheses.
validated_scope.width: The actual scalar minimum enters WidthComparisonData and yields the CM right-slope estimate and existing width deadline, conditional on those comparison data. No geometric sweepout or varifold realization is asserted.
validated_scope.coordinates: The existing parameter change identities remain available. The induced metric on a smooth immersed surface now also gives exactly the original surfaceMetricMatrix, surfaceDensity and patchArea after composition with a differentiable parameter map. Global area uses DifferentialGeometry's Riemannian measure on the domain; the new patch compatibility theorem compares the two local density integrals.
validated_scope.closed_surface: For a fixed smooth immersion of a compact boundaryless surface, construct its actual induced metric and global area measure, prove finite area and positivity for a nonempty domain, and derive HasDerivAt of total area under an actual IsSolutionOn Ricci flow at every regular time. The derivative is minus the integral of the ambient Ricci tensor traced using the induced metric. Joint regularity is derived from the solution predicate; no additional domination, global-in-time regularity, global frame, normal vector field, or injectivity of the map itself is assumed. Branch points and Sobolev maps are not covered.

remaining_inputs: Construct the required Ricci-flow solution and its regularity from a compatible initial metric.
Extend global surface area and its variation to the branched and Sobolev maps used by CM, including estimates uniform over almost-maximal sweepout slices.

Upgrade and review the existing Petersen second fundamental form and Gauss-Codazzi implementation, identify its tangential curvature with the actual induced metric, and supply the branched Gauss-Bonnet theorem.
Construct manifold-valued Sobolev maps, sweepouts, harmonic replacement and the min-max comparison families.
Prove compatibility of geometric widths, curvature bounds and topological records with surgery.
blueprint_note: The introductory claim of area loss at least 4*pi per unit time needs the scalar-curvature correction. The valid minimal-sphere bound is A′ <= -4*pi - R_min*A/2, including the branch-point treatment required by CM.

differential_geometry_boundary.scope: Boundary second fundamental form; symmetry assumes symmetric chart coefficients. This does not supply the intrinsic Gauss equation for an arbitrary immersed surface.
